text.p: Nutrition For Life International Inc said on Tuesday it reached preliminary settlements for two class actions suits filed in 1996.

The company said it agreed to set aside a reserve fund of between $1.2 million and $1.5 million as part of the settlement of one suit. Any amounts left in the reserve fund will be refunded to the company six months after the final approval of the settlement pact, the company said.

Also as part of this first settlement, the company said it agreed to offer products with a retail value equivalent to the amount of any expired unredeemed certificates held. The cost of the products and shipping will equal about $800,000, the company said.
Nutrition For Life said it will pay up to $2 million in the second class action suit to people who bought its common stock and warrants between July 11, 1995, and July 15,1995, and lost money.

The company, which said it denies all allegations of securities law violations, was accused in an August 1996, lawsuit of engaging in an illegal pyramid scheme. Its system of "executive-level" distributor program was also the subject of a probe by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission until early December.
